title: Why your recorded voice sounds weird
description:
Ever wondered why your voice sounds so different and squeaky on recordings? Here is the science behind bone conduction and how other people actually hear you.
#science #voice #shorts #didyouknow

scenes.narration: Hate your recorded voice? Blame your bones.
scenes.imagePrompt: cinematic close-up of a young person listening to a voice recording on a smartphone, puzzled expression, dark room lit only by the phone screen, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: When you speak, sound reaches your inner ears through two separate paths.
scenes.imagePrompt: macro shot of a human ear with soft glowing sound waves flowing around it, dark background, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: The first is through the air, just like everyone else hears. The second is through your skull bones.
scenes.imagePrompt: glowing sound wave lines passing through a translucent human head silhouette, side view, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Your bones enhance low frequencies, making your voice sound deeper and richer inside your head.
scenes.imagePrompt: x-ray style image of a human skull with warm low-frequency waves glowing inside, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: A microphone only picks up airborne sound. Without the bone vibrations, you sound higher and totally unfamiliar.
scenes.imagePrompt: close-up of a studio condenser microphone in a dark room, a thin bright sound wave in front of it, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Psychologists studied this back in the nineteen sixties. Hearing your true voice triggers pure discomfort.
scenes.imagePrompt: person in headphones covering face with one hand in mild embarrassment, dim recording studio, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: The good news is, that recording is what everyone hears every day. They are used to it, and you can get used to it too.
scenes.imagePrompt: group of friends talking and laughing at a cafe table at night, warm bokeh lights in the background, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Do you actually like the sound of your recorded voice?
